entry.title: [bijanabdolkarimi] "Let us not be fooled by some so-called reformist leaders who are secretly out…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @bijanabdolkarimi

"Let us not be fooled by some so-called reformist leaders who are secretly out to destroy society, nor by some principlists who have lately become more reformist (read: more destructive) than the reformists themselves."

Some in Iran, without decoding the philosophy of the US government and the role of the disaster-driven capitalist system in shaping that government's long-term orientations, claim that it is Iranians who are averse to compromise with America and are warmongering?!

Noam Chomsky, one of the greatest contemporary American philosophers, in his book "Understanding Power," citing more than 130 different historical cases of how America and Israel have trespassed and aggressed against other countries, especially in the Middle East, shows that America, in its dealings with others, arranges conditions in such a way that negotiation and compromise become impossible, and subsequently America, on the pretext that the other side has refused to negotiate and compromise, proceeds to missile strikes and genocide against others.

So why do some reformists and principlists claim that Iranians are warmongering and the US government is peace-loving?! This issue must be viewed within the framework of political economy, of pointing people in the wrong direction, of concealing the inefficiency of domestic management, and of making life more expensive for the people.

✍Yavar Ahmadpour Torkamani
